label: reset drops its last argument
reset does not clear eventCode
the two echo durations are added the other way round
why: The object reads +0x88 into %ecx and +0x8c into %eax and immediately does `add %ecx,%eax` at .text+0x16beb; neither field is read anywhere else in any of this class's thirteen symbols, so only the SUM reaches any store.  No observable in the object, let alone in this harness, can order two addends.  The argument expires the moment some other member reads one of the two fields on its own.

label: the product is kept in double rather than narrowed to float
why: The float intermediate is derived from the ENCODING and not from a test: .text+0x16c65 stores the double product as four bytes (`fstps`) and +0x16c69 loads it back (`flds`) before +0x16c6d adds a FOUR-byte 0.5, neither of which a double expression throughout would need.  It is unobservable because `reset` sets `codeLevel` to the literal 4000 and no symbol of this class writes that field otherwise, so 4000 is the only input: 4000*sqrt(3/2) is 4898.979485566356, its float rounding is 4898.97949, and both give 4899 after +0.5 and truncation.  The argument expires if any caller ever gives the object another codeLevel.

ctor: the level argument is 1000, not 4000
why: `reset`'s first parameter is DEAD.  The amplitude is `reset`'s own literal -- `movw $0xfa0,0x4(%esi)` in both tail-duplicated blocks, .text+0x16c35 and +0x16cc1 -- and the argument's slot at 0x24(%esp) is never read.  The reconstruction reproduces that with `(void)levelArg`, so no value passed here can reach the object and no test in this tree can tell 4000 from 1000.  The constant is kept because it is what the object passes, not because it does anything.
